speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with persistent vomiting and chest pain; to start our evaluation, have these symptoms been present for more than 24 hours, and do you have any history of heart disease or recent trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture)

The patient's history of forceful retching followed by chest pain and choking after heavy alcohol consumption is classic for esophageal rupture. Given the inability to communicate effectively, please prepare for an immediate emergency chest X-ray and a contrast esophagram to confirm the diagnosis.
